references.text: Psalm 22:6-8 contains a prophecy describing how the Messiah will be mocked and ridiculed, reflecting the situation where Jesus' charge title, 'King of the Jews,' is used to mock him.

In Matthew 27:37 we find a parallel event where it is also mentioned that the charge title 'This is Jesus, the King of the Jews' was placed above Jesus' head, which directly corresponds to the event in Mark 15:26.
Luke 23:38 also describes how an inscription reading 'This is the King of the Jews' was placed above Jesus, which is a direct parallel to Mark 15:26.
John 19:19 mentions that Pilate wrote a title and put it on the cross, 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews,' which is another direct parallel to the event described in Mark 15:26.

Isaiah 53:3-12 is a prophecy about the suffering servant, which many interpret as a prediction of Jesus' suffering and death, including how he was perceived and treated by his own people, something that can be seen in connection with the description of Jesus as 'the King of the Jews' in Mark 15:26.
